name: Lead (Pb)
summary: A toxic heavy metal with no safe exposure level. It interferes with enzymes (notably in haem synthesis), mimics calcium, and is especially harmful to the developing brain.

conditions.label: Toxicity / exposure
conditions.description: Lead disrupts haem synthesis and neuronal signalling and deposits in bone; children absorb and are harmed by it far more than adults.

affects.effect: Encephalopathy and loss of IQ / cognition
affects.detail: Lead disrupts neurotransmission and synaptic pruning. High levels cause encephalopathy, seizures and coma; even low chronic exposure lowers IQ and attention.

ageModifiers.infant: The developing brain is exquisitely sensitive; there is no identified safe blood-lead level in children.
ageModifiers.child: Causes irreversible deficits in IQ, attention and behaviour, plus developmental delay.
ageModifiers.adult: Chronic exposure causes headache, memory loss, peripheral neuropathy (wrist/foot drop) and mood change.

affects.detail: Lead inhibits ALA dehydratase and ferrochelatase in haem synthesis, causing anaemia and basophilic stippling of red cells.
Chronic exposure damages proximal tubules (Fanconi-like) and, over years, causes interstitial nephritis and chronic kidney disease.
Lead mimics calcium and is stored in bone for decades; dense metaphyseal 'lead lines' are visible on children's X-rays.
Acute exposure causes crampy abdominal pain ('lead colic'), anorexia and constipation.
